entries.title: passmcp — test any MCP server, from your own machine
entries.content:
Skip to main content passmcp Menu System Running locally · nothing leaves this machineTest an MCP server.Nine phases, 138 checks, both protocol generations. Every finding is tied to the request that produced it, and the whole run happens here — the endpoint, the credentials and the report never leave this machine.Run a diagnostic9phases, in order138checksBothprotocol revisions, detected0bytes uploadedConnectWhere to look, and what to authenticate with. Both the handshake revisions and 2026-07-28 are detected from the server itself — there is nothing to choose.MCP server endpoint The Streamable HTTP URL. The checks that watch the server process itself (its stdio behaviour, where it connects, the files it touches and what its binary is built from) need a server that is a program rather than a URL; run those from the command line with passmcp check --stdio -- .Credentials Auto-detectNoneBearer tokenOAuth client credentialsStored loginToken from environment variable A name, not a token. The browser sends the variable's name. passmcp reads the value on this machine, uses it against the server you named, and never writes it into the report. Nothing here reaches anybody else's infrastructure. SafetyOnly tools declaring readOnlyHint are called. Everything here is an explicit opt-in, and belongs to a server you own.Safety opt-ins Also call tools that mutate but are not destructive Also call destructive and unannotated tools Skip the protocol-generation probe (one fewer request)ToolsThe same selector passmcp check -i draws in a terminal. Choosing a tool is an explicit opt-in, so picking a mutating one widens the policy for that tool and nothing else.List this server’s tools Tools to exerciseWith nothing selected, every tool the policy already permits is exercised, which is what a run does by default.PacingA scheduled diagnostic against somebody's production server is a load test if you let it be.Requests per second 0 removes the throttle.Per-call timeout (seconds) Per call, not per run.Run diagnostic Cancel Enter an endpoint to begin.ProgressEach phase reports as it finishes. Findings appear beneath the phase that produced them.ResultOpen the full report Download JSON The full report prints to PDF from your browser.

This page runs diagnostics in your browser and needs JavaScript. Without it, use the command line: passmcp check https://mcp.example.com/mcp
